customer_reviews.title: Mighty %26 fast!
customer_reviews.review: Anker has reached a pretty reputable status at this point. With that said, this power bank is really a big hefty beast. It has weight to it, and conveniently comes with its own carrying pouch. The included pouch makes this hefty power bank even more portable. The pouch has enough space to house the power bank and a few cables (like 2 or 3). With 20.000 mAh of power, you can be assured that the Anker power bank will keep your devices powered when traveling or even during emergencies (like power outages caused by severe weather). The amount of charges the bank can offer all depend on how many devices you charge and their required sustenance. Another detail I'd like to add is the impressive speed at which the bank can both recharge and power other devices! It is rated to power devices up to 140 watts and recharge the device itself up to 140 watts. In order to take advantage of this particular feature, I recommend you to use a USB C cable capable of outputting 140 watts or more. Likewise, whenever the bank's battery drains and needs to recharge, I too recommend a 140 watt capable USB C cable so that the power bank could recharge to 100% in just 30 minutes. Do keep in mind however, that when recharging the power bank, you use a power outlet/block capable of outputting 140 watts. Anything lower will increase re-charge time. I can confirm that the power bank can re-charge at relatively fast speeds using an output of 100 watts though. It took about 45-50 minutes for my power bank to go from 0% to 100% by using said output. Using your cell-phone's block charger can juice up the Anker power bank, but it will most likely take hours before it can reach 100%. Overall a great power bank with impressive charge %26 re-charge speeds, as long as you have the cables/power blocks capable of outputting at least 140 watts.

customer_reviews.title: It’s Apple! Do I need to say more?
customer_reviews.review:
My son owned the AirPod Pro 2 model. He loved ‘em. My wife has some hearing loss. She broke her very expensive hearing aids. So I decided to let her try my son’s AirPod Pro 2 with the “Hearing Aid” feature enabled while streaming movies together on our TV. She heard every word perfectly.

customer_reviews.name: Russell
customer_reviews.title: Unbelievable sound, but completely unreliable
customer_reviews.review:
OK, I'm a huge fan of Bose, but I would love to see them catch up the software with the technology. I have had almost every earbuds they make in the last 6 years, and they were all top tear. The sound is amazing. I'm not an audiophile, so it doesn't help me when I read reviews about the mids, the highs, and the different types of audio  filesit plays. I just want to know do they sound great? (Unbelievable) How long does the battery last? (On par with advertized time) Are they comfy? Very. Though I can't lay in bed with my head sideways on the pillow because they stick out of my ear) Will they stay in my ears? (100%)  Are they water resistant in case I sweat, get caught in the rain, or accidentally jump in the shower because they are so comfortable and sound so realistic and natural that I forgot I was wearing them? (Lowest ranting of water resistance) How's the noise canceling? (So good it's spooky)

But the last few years, there have been consistent faults with the software not working correctly, having to reset the earbuds, or having to delete the app and re-download it. It's frequent for me for them to disconnect then reconnect, or for one earbuds to disconnect. I'm very frustrated with this at the moment, and I'm baffled as to why Bose can't or won't fix this.

customer_reviews.review:
Not as good is the first generation from the Quiet perspective. Not sure what the issue is, technology or perhaps the eartips/stability bands are not as good as the eartips from the first generation for blocking out extra noise. Have tried different combinations of the various eartips/stabnility band sizes, but either caused the earbuds to fall out or didn't seem to physically block out noise. 

On a positive note, the sound is better.

Rather disappointing and not sure they are worth the money.

positive.review:
I decided that it was time to upgrade to a really great set of wireless, circumoral headphones.  Lots of great choices out there right now, but I narrowed my list down to the Sony® WH-1000XM5, or the Apple® Airpods Max.

I tested both.  Both sound fantastic, and worth the high price.

But I went with Sony.

>> Sound quality is 100% first class. All the frequencies are in perfect balance, and the difficult-to-get-right midrange is studio-perfect.

>> Packed with peerless technology, e.g. the headphones know when they are on or off your head, and when off they can automatically pause whatever you're listening to.

>> The active noise cancelling is absolutely superb.  Press a button and all exterior sounds are gone. For me, this feature works better than physical ear plugs, believe it or not.

>> Control the volume and other settings with gestures.  Swipe up and down on the right-side cup for volume control, etc. You also have the option to use voice commands.

>> Not 1, not 2 -- 8 microphones!  So you can make calls with these babies with 100% confidence.  This microphone abundance contributes much to the excellent active noise cancelling.

A bit disappointed that Sony decided to go with a plastic frame with instead of metal with WH-1000XM5. The Airpods Max headphones have a steel frame.  The plastic parts of my old (and legendary) Sony MDR V6 headphones actually started to crumble after a few years.  Steel doesn't have that problem.

Also disappointing:  The Sony Headphone Connect app is for mobile devices only.  I am a PC man.   A PC version would have been optimal.

NB1: As with all Apple products, headphone features work great with Apple software and hardware, and have certain drawbacks when used with PCs.  Sony doesn't have that drawback, and I am a Windows / PC person.

NB2: A full charge will give you 30 hours a play with the Sony WH-1000XM5. Apple Airpods Max = 20 hours with a full charge.
